polityNote: First-level units of the Republic of Uzbekistan from the dissolution of the USSR (26 Dec 1991) to the restoration of Navoi oblast (27 Jan 1992). In this month there was no Navoi oblast — its districts were in Bukhara and Samarkand — and Yangiabad was in Syrdarya; the Natural Earth fill drew the modern 14 units. Atoms: geoBoundaries UZB ADM2 (OCHA 2020, 199 districts and towns, 17,848 vertices; a clean partition, 0 overlaps at 0.01°). Check ① (geodesic area of the union against stated areas): Samarkand with Nurata and Khatirchi 25,378 km² vs 16,770 + 6,500 + 1,382 = 24,652 km² = 1.03; Bukhara with the six Navoi districts 145,284 km² vs 40,320 + 110,800 − 7,882 = 143,238 km² = 1.01. The OCHA lines and the OSM 2017 first-level lines disagree most along the Amu Darya (Khorezm 5,276 km² in OCHA against 6,828 km² in OSM); the river line is the publisher’s, not reconstructed here. OpenHistoricalMap carries only the country for these years.

spans.dateNote: With the six former Navoi districts returned on 16 May 1989 (Navoi/Karmana, Kanimekh, Kyzyltepa, Tamdy, Uchkuduk; Navbahor restored inside in 1990). Uchkuduk is not named in the 1989 sources; it is assigned to Bukhara by contiguity — it touches only Tamdy and Kanimekh (both Bukharan then), Karakalpakstan, Kazakhstan and Bukharan Peshku, so in Samarkand it would have been a detached exclave. The 2018 transfer from Gijduvan to Kanimekh moved land between two districts that were both Bukharan in 1991, so the union is unchanged. Navoi and Zarafshan towns are withheld (unresolved).
